## cfoai
# cfo.ai MCP

You are connected to **cfo.ai** — an AI-native financial planning workspace. This MCP exposes Ari's public product tools for you to call directly. You can both **read** a company's financial model and **change** it: create and edit scenarios, pages, table blocks, Canvas blocks, formulas, variables, dimensions, and data ingestion.

Model-editing tools change the live model immediately and record reversible changes in its
changelog. Connections, access changes, and outbound actions have effects outside model undo. Build from saved data, research, supplied numbers, estimates, hypotheses, or invented
assumptions. Clearly label uncited inputs and their basis in the model and handoff. Create missing
model objects and editable inputs as part of the work. A missing source citation does not block modeling.

## Read the reference before you build

cfo.ai has its own modeling method, described under "How a table shows the model" below: how tables show variables, dimensions, and fields, how a reference reads from the cell it sits in, and how a table's rows and columns are built. `inspect_skills` owns the built-in and workspace skill catalog. Use its `list` block to find a skill and its `instructions` block to read it.

Read `build-model` before creating or changing model logic, variables, dimensions, or saved tables;
`build-visualizations` before adding a Canvas block; and `import-model` before rebuilding a model
from a workbook or export. Each manual contains its complete reference in `SKILL.md`.

Workspace skills hold company-specific playbooks. Read the relevant saved guidance before substantial work.

## Calling convention

- A multi-action tool selects one operation with the block named for that action; single-purpose tools use their fields directly. Supply only fields supported inside the selected block. An `inspect_*` tool reads saved product state; an `edit_*` tool changes it.
- `target` identifies an existing object where the operation needs one, including the destination of a new block. Creation fields describe the new object: use the selected operation's `name`, `title`, `source`, or other published fields. On an update, `name` gives the selected object's new name.
- Supply `org_id` when selecting a workspace by ID or slug. If you belong to exactly one workspace, the server selects it automatically. Use `list_orgs` when the correct workspace is unclear.
- Tools accept an optional `_context` object — `{ layerId, pageId, timeZone, utcOffset }` — that mirrors the in-app editing context. Supply `layerId` for the active scenario, `pageId` for the current page, and `timeZone` or `utcOffset` when relative dates matter. Identify existing objects by readable names or references returned by an inspection.
- Model object selectors accept names, returned `Name#hex` disambiguators, or IDs unless the field states a narrower contract. A returned `Name#a1b` carries a prefix of the object's identity, at least three hex digits and unique among every object of its kind when the result was written; later creates can lengthen it, so a reference from an older result resolves while it stays unique, and a fresh inspection carries the current spelling. Ambiguous or unknown names return candidates when available. Each tool defines singular or plural targets, omitted/empty/null input behavior, and scenario defaults.
- Reuse pagination cursors unchanged with the same tool, action, target, filters, and snapshot. Each cursor field names the returned value to use and any special empty-string behavior.
- A saved table is created or reshaped with its complete visible `rows` and `columns`. A dimension path may use a bounded member `filter`, an ancestor `when` condition, or independent sibling `branches`. Inspection returns the same saved shape under `layout.rows` and `layout.columns`. Updates use `row_updates`, `column_updates`, and `cell_updates`. An `add_dimension_items` entry places a planned member `under` an existing inspected parent.
- A Canvas block reads model values through named `datasets`. Each dataset declares the same visible sh… [truncated]

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

## 5. Sponsor integrations (in the loop)

### neatlogs (agent observability)
- `pip install "neatlogs[litellm]"`. Call `neatlogs.init(api_key=env NEATLOGS_API_KEY, workflow_name="heirloom", instrumentations=["litellm"], tags=[...])` **before importing litellm**, and `neatlogs.flush(); neatlogs.shutdown()` on exit.
- **Sessions:** `with neatlogs.identify(session_id=f"campaign-{run}")` for the campaign. Each CVE gets `identify(session_id=f"cve-{id}-{run}", parent_session_id=f"campaign-{run}")`.
- **Spans:** `with neatlogs.trace("<stage>", kind="AGENT|TOOL|GUARDRAIL") as span: span.set_attribute(...)`.
  - Always set (explicit values, never missing): `heirloom.cve`, `heirloom.line`, `heirloom.stage`, `heirloom.verdict`, `heirloom.calibrated`, `heirloom.reach`, `heirloom.reason`, `heirloom.tests_edited_after_red`, `heirloom.claims_unlinked`, `heirloom.cost_usd`, `heirloom.claim_id`.
  - Wrap each `claude -p` run in an AGENT span carrying its `total_cost_usd`, `session_id` and checkpoint id (headless calls bypass the LiteLLM instrumentation).
- **Detections** (Public API `https://app.neatlogs.com/api/v1/public`, headers `Authorization: Bearer $NEATLOGS_SERVICE_TOKEN`, `x-project-id: $NEATLOGS_PROJECT_ID`, `idempotency-key`).
  - Create **conditional** detections on span attributes **before the v1 baseline runs**: `not_affected_without_calibration`, `fix_applied_where_probe_passed`, `probe_never_reached_region`, `claim_without_span`, `test_edited_after_red`.
  - Read `GET /detections/{id}/hits` and `/trends?granularity=hour` for the before/after chart. Check the conditional config syntax with `neatlogs schema search` or the docs first.
  - Backfill is not available on our tier; don't depend on it.
- **MCP:** the agent may call `search_traces` / `get_trace_context` (`https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp`, Bearer project key) to look up past failures of the same class (env build, flaky module) and reuse the recovery.

### Entire (agent sessions as git checkpoints)
- **Build time:** this repo has `entire enable --agent claude-code`. Use Entire deliberately and record the outputs in `hackathon.md`:
  - `entire status`, `entire checkpoint list`, `entire checkpoint explain <id>`;
  - `entire graph impact` (after `entire plugin install graph`);
  - `entire review` on a branch;
  - `entire recap`.
- **Runtime:** for each fork worktree, run `entire enable --agent claude-code --yes --local --telemetry=false`. Add `"commit_linking": "always"` to `.entire/settings.local.json`, and add `.claude/` and `.entire/` to `.git/info/exclude`.
  - After the orchestrator commits, check `git log -1 --format=%B | grep '^Entire-Checkpoint:'` and record the checkpoint id. Push the checkpoint refs with the branch. The PR links the checkpoint.
  - If trailers don't appear in headless mode, the fallback is an Agent Integration Protocol plugin `entire-agent-heirloom` (subcommands: info, detect, get-session-id, get-session-dir, resolve-session-file, read-session, write-session, read-transcript, chunk-transcript, reassemble-transcript, format-resume-command). Only if time allows.

### cfo.ai (business plan)
Done through the cfo.ai MCP in a session with that MCP connected. Inputs must be **measured**: cost per CVE from neatlogs/ledger, EC2 $/hour, human minutes per escalation.
- **Pricing hypotheses:** per verified backport, and a per-package-line monthly subscription for distro/ELTS teams.
- Scenarios base/bear/bull, a runway view, and a shared Page.
- Export a summary to `docs/business-plan.md` with the Page link.

## 6. Evals (real ground truth; numbers only from runs)
### 10.7 Outreach drafts (never filed by the agent; the human files each one)
Write drafts to `docs/outreach/`, each built only from confirmed artifacts:
- `ubuntu-cve-2026-87890.md`: Launchpad bug text for python-django (noble). Contents: facts with links, calibrated probe results, candidate patch.
- `debian-cve-2026-53878.md`: security-tracker correction proposal with the provenance proof.
- `neatlogs-pii-dlq.md`: issue with a minimal repro of large-attribute spans stalling at pii_redaction.
- `entire-empty-repo-session.md`: issue: a session started before the first commit is never tracked ("failed to get HEAD").

**Required wording for the Ubuntu draft:** "noble's CVE-2026-15307 backport leaves the bytes path that upstream closed as CVE-2026-87890; our calibrated probe shows it." No exploitability claim. No jammy claim unless a 3.2 line was actually run.

## 5. Sponsor integrations (in the loop)

### neatlogs (agent observability)
- `pip install "neatlogs[litellm]"`. Call `neatlogs.init(api_key=env NEATLOGS_API_KEY, workflow_name="heirloom", instrumentations=["litellm"], tags=[...])` **before importing litellm**, and `neatlogs.flush(); neatlogs.shutdown()` on exit.
- **Sessions:** `with neatlogs.identify(session_id=f"campaign-{run}")` for the campaign. Each CVE gets `identify(session_id=f"cve-{id}-{run}", parent_session_id=f"campaign-{run}")`.
- **Spans:** `with neatlogs.trace("<stage>", kind="AGENT|TOOL|GUARDRAIL") as span: span.set_attribute(...)`.
  - Always set (explicit values, never missing): `heirloom.cve`, `heirloom.line`, `heirloom.stage`, `heirloom.verdict`, `heirloom.calibrated`, `heirloom.reach`, `heirloom.reason`, `heirloom.tests_edited_after_red`, `heirloom.claims_unlinked`, `heirloom.cost_usd`, `heirloom.claim_id`.
  - Wrap each `claude -p` run in an AGENT span carrying its `total_cost_usd`, `session_id` and checkpoint id (headless calls bypass the LiteLLM instrumentation).
- **Detections** (Public API `https://app.neatlogs.com/api/v1/public`, headers `Authorization: Bearer $NEATLOGS_SERVICE_TOKEN`, `x-project-id: $NEATLOGS_PROJECT_ID`, `idempotency-key`).
  - Create **conditional** detections on span attributes **before the v1 baseline runs**: `not_affected_without_calibration`, `fix_applied_where_probe_passed`, `probe_never_reached_region`, `claim_without_span`, `test_edited_after_red`.
  - Read `GET /detections/{id}/hits` and `/trends?granularity=hour` for the before/after chart. Check the conditional config syntax with `neatlogs schema search` or the docs first.
  - Backfill is not available on our tier; don't depend on it.
- **MCP:** the agent may call `search_traces` / `get_trace_context` (`https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp`, Bearer project key) to look up past failures of the same class (env build, flaky module) and reuse the recovery.

### Entire (agent sessions as git checkpoints)
- **Build time:** this repo has `entire enable --agent claude-code`. Use Entire deliberately and record the outputs in `hackathon.md`:
  - `entire status`, `entire checkpoint list`, `entire checkpoint explain <id>`;
  - `entire graph impact` (after `entire plugin install graph`);
  - `entire review` on a branch;
  - `entire recap`.
- **Runtime:** for each fork worktree, run `entire enable --agent claude-code --yes --local --telemetry=false`. Add `"commit_linking": "always"` to `.entire/settings.local.json`, and add `.claude/` and `.entire/` to `.git/info/exclude`.
  - After the orchestrator commits, check `git log -1 --format=%B | grep '^Entire-Checkpoint:'` and record the checkpoint id. Push the checkpoint refs with the branch. The PR links the checkpoint.
  - If trailers don't appear in headless mode, the fallback is an Agent Integration Protocol plugin `entire-agent-heirloom` (subcommands: info, detect, get-session-id, get-session-dir, resolve-session-file, read-session, write-session, read-transcript, chunk-transcript, reassemble-transcript, format-resume-command). Only if time allows.

### cfo.ai (business plan)
Done through the cfo.ai MCP in a session with that MCP connected. Inputs must be **measured**: cost per CVE from neatlogs/ledger, EC2 $/hour, human minutes per escalation.
- **Pricing hypotheses:** per verified backport, and a per-package-line monthly subscription for distro/ELTS teams.
- Scenarios base/bear/bull, a runway view, and a shared Page.
- Export a summary to `docs/business-plan.md` with the Page link.

## 6. Evals (real ground truth; numbers only from runs)
### 10.7 Outreach drafts (never filed by the agent; the human files each one)
Write drafts to `docs/outreach/`, each built only from confirmed artifacts:
- `ubuntu-cve-2026-87890.md`: Launchpad bug text for python-django (noble). Contents: facts with links, calibrated probe results, candidate patch.
- `debian-cve-2026-53878.md`: security-tracker correction proposal with the provenance proof.
- `neatlogs-pii-dlq.md`: issue with a minimal repro of large-attribute spans stalling at pii_redaction.
- `entire-empty-repo-session.md`: issue: a session started before the first commit is never tracked ("failed to get HEAD").

**Required wording for the Ubuntu draft:** "noble's CVE-2026-15307 backport leaves the bytes path that upstream closed as CVE-2026-87890; our calibrated probe shows it." No exploitability claim. No jammy claim unless a 3.2 line was actually run.

entire checkpoint explain — Explain a session, commit, or checkpoint
Explain provides human-readable context about sessions, commits, and checkpoints.

Use this command to understand what happened during agent-driven development,
either for self-review or to understand a teammate's work.

By default, shows checkpoints on the current branch. Pass a checkpoint ID or
commit SHA as a positional argument to explain a specific item, or use flags.

Viewing specific items:
  entire checkpoint explain <id-or-sha>           Auto-detects checkpoint ID or commit SHA
  entire checkpoint explain --checkpoint <id>     Force interpretation as checkpoint ID
  entire checkpoint explain --commit <ref>        Force interpretation as commit ref

Checkpoints in another repo:
  entire checkpoint explain <id> --repo gh/owner/name
  entire checkpoint explain <id> --repo et/project/repo
                 Explain a checkpoint owned by another repository — the
                 drill-down for a cross-repo 'entire search' hit. Reads it from
                 that repo's Entire API; nothing is written to this repo.
                 Needs a full checkpoint ID (positional or --checkpoint) and a
                 checkpoint that has been pushed.

Filtering the list view:
  --session      Filter checkpoints by session ID (or prefix)

Output verbosity levels (when explaining a specific item):
  Default:         Detailed view with scoped prompts (ID, session, tokens, intent, prompts, files)
  --short          Summary only (ID, session, timestamp, tokens, intent)
  --full           Parsed full transcript (all prompts/responses from entire session)

"""Spike S4: emit one matching + one non-matching 'calibrate' span, plus one LiteLLM call."""
import os, sys, time
from dotenv import load_dotenv

load_dotenv("/home/ubuntu/heirloom/.env")
import neatlogs  # noqa: E402

RUN = sys.argv[1]
neatlogs.init(api_key=os.environ["NEATLOGS_API_KEY"], workflow_name="heirloom",
              instrumentations=["litellm"], tags=["spike-s4", f"run-{RUN}"])
import litellm  # noqa: E402  (must come after neatlogs.init)

ATTRS = dict(line="4.2", stage="calibrate", reach=True, reason="", tests_edited_after_red=False,
             claims_unlinked=0, cost_usd=0.0)

def calibrate_span(cve, verdict, calibrated, claim):
    with neatlogs.trace(f"cve-{cve}", kind="AGENT"), neatlogs.trace("calibrate", kind="GUARDRAIL") as span:
        span.set_attribute("heirloom.cve", cve)
        span.set_attribute("heirloom.verdict", verdict)
        span.set_attribute("heirloom.calibrated", calibrated)
        span.set_attribute("heirloom.claim_id", claim)
        for k, v in ATTRS.items():
            span.set_attribute(f"heirloom.{k}", v)
        ctx = span.get_span_context() if hasattr(span, "get_span_context") else None
        return format(ctx.trace_id, "032x") if ctx else None, format(ctx.span_id, "016x") if ctx else None

try:
    with neatlogs.identify(session_id=f"campaign-s4-{RUN}"):
        with neatlogs.identify(session_id=f"cve-CVE-SPIKE-MATCH-{RUN}"):
            print("match   ", calibrate_span("CVE-SPIKE-MATCH", "NOT_AFFECTED_PROVEN", False, "c-match"))
        with neatlogs.identify(session_id=f"cve-CVE-SPIKE-CLEAN-{RUN}"):
            print("nomatch ", calibrate_span("CVE-SPIKE-CLEAN", "AFFECTED", True, "c-clean"))
            r = litellm.completion(model="openai/claude-haiku", api_base="https://litellm.vision.aivar.app/v1",
                                   api_key=os.environ["LITELLM_API_KEY"], max_tokens=5,
                                   messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say ok."}])
            print("litellm ", r.choices[0].message.content, r.usage.total_tokens)
finally:
    print("flush", neatlogs.flush())
    neatlogs.shutdown()
